sentences.show: This probe was built to float, in case Venus had water. Its lock was made of sugar.
Venera 4 reached Venus on this day in 1967.
No one knew what lay under the clouds, so its designers allowed for a landing in water.
The sugar would dissolve, and release the antennas.
It hit the atmosphere so hard, its heat shield reached 11,000 degrees.
Then the parachute opened, and for the first time, a probe tasted the air of another planet.
It was almost all carbon dioxide.
As it fell, the heat rose to 262 degrees, the pressure to 22 atmospheres.
Moscow first announced it had reached the surface. A radar quirk had fooled them.
There was no water. At the ground, Venus is hotter than an oven — 467 degrees.
Three years later, Venera 7 finally touched down.
Also on this day: Perón married Evita, and an earthquake destroyed Basel.
Our app is still on its way down. Subscribe, and be there the moment it lands.
